searchText: Preston and I have the following concern: We don't use attestations that are in the blocks for fork choice It's likely that an attestation could be missing in its gossip domain but later showed up inside a block Given that, we are thinking to track which attestation is procssed, and if there's an attestation showed up in the block which we haven't seen before, we'll apply fork choice for that yeah exactly, if we learn of an attestation we haven't seen before through a new block, why would we ignore this data for fork choice? Adding more information expands our view of the world and it doesn't make sense to ignore data because it's already been processed in a block **cem_ozer** (in reply to **<@363800010518822915>**) Are you sure that’s correct? I believed that we applied any attestation that we receive over the wire, which is not a duplicate, to the fork choice "attestation that receive over the wire" meaning it can be the attestations when we unpack the block? **cem_ozer** I think so **cem_ozer** It shouldnt matter where you receive the attestation as long as you know its valid imo makes sense to me I dont think we have this in the spec today Yeah, whether gossiped directly or inside a block or received hand delivered by snailmail to your server, you should incorporate the attestation into your fork choice. I suppose `on_attestation` should include a note that said attestations can come from any source **cem_ozer** (in reply to **<@291925846556540928>**) “hand delivered by snailmail to your server” 😂😂😂 As long as it's well aggregated. I'd take them 😆

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: Preston and I have the following concern:

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: We don't use attestations that are in the blocks for fork choice

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: It's likely that an attestation could be missing in its gossip domain but later showed up inside a block

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: Given that, we are thinking to track which attestation is procssed, and if there's an attestation showed up in the block which we haven't seen before, we'll apply fork choice for that

excerpts.author: prestonvanloon
excerpts.content: yeah exactly, if we learn of an attestation we haven't seen before through a new block, why would we ignore this data for fork choice? Adding more information expands our view of the world and it doesn't make sense to ignore data because it's already been processed in a block

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content: Are you sure that’s correct? I believed that we applied any attestation that we receive over the wire, which is not a duplicate, to the fork choice

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: "attestation that receive over the wire" meaning it can be the attestations when we unpack the block?

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**cem_ozer**
It shouldnt matter where you receive the attestation as long as you know its valid imo

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: I dont think we have this in the spec today

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: Yeah, whether gossiped directly or inside a block or received hand delivered by snailmail to your server, you should incorporate the attestation into your fork choice. I suppose `on_attestation` should include a note that said attestations can come from any source

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content: “hand delivered by snailmail to your server” 😂😂😂

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: As long as it's well aggregated. I'd take them 😆
